data.case_title: Dubious invoice from "Grundstücksregister Online Service GmbH"
data.title: Invoice for a private property registry listing (Eintragung Grundstücksregister)
data.summary: Grundstücksregister Online Service GmbH, a private company, sent an invoice for €498.00 for a two-year "registration" of the property at Ackerstraße 26, Mustermünster, due by 1 December 2026. The letter itself states it is only an offer, unrelated to the official land registry (Grundbuch), and that a contract only comes into existence if payment is made.
data.explanation: This letter looks like an official invoice but is actually a commercial offer from a private company, not a government agency. It explicitly says no contract exists unless you pay, and the "registration" has nothing to do with the real, official land registry (Grundbuch). Letters like this are a known pattern used to trick property owners into paying for a worthless private listing. You are not legally obliged to pay anything. If you don't want this service, simply do not pay and keep the letter as a record; if you already paid or feel pressured, you can contact a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) for help.

items.title: Decide whether to pay for the private registry listing
items.action: Decide if you want this optional private property listing; you are not legally required to pay, since the letter itself says no contract exists until payment.
items.consequence: No consequence is stated for not paying, since the letter explains a contract only forms if you pay.

warnings: This resembles a known German scam pattern: a private company disguises a non-binding commercial offer as an official land-registry invoice; the letter itself admits it has no connection to the real Grundbuch and no contract exists unless you pay.
Do not treat this as a legal obligation; if unsure, contact a consumer advice centre (Verbraucherzentrale) before paying.
